newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock exchange rises on Mideast optimism.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock exchange rises on Mideast optimism.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose 0.45 percent on Tuesday in quiet trade boosted by optimism over Middle East peace talks and an Iraqi pledge that it wanted to continue supplying Jordan with cheap oil, brokers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.69 points to 153.00 points in turnover worth 342,000 dinars ($483,000). Trade in the Moslem holy month of Ramadan is traditionally light, with few buyers around.
Brokers said market confidence, sensitive to political developments in the region, was boosted by expectations that Israel and the Palestinians were close to signing a new accord.
Aziz's comments also cheered brokers, although he questioned Jordanian statements that Baghdad was deeply in debt to Amman.
"The market had been expected to respond more positively than it did," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments.
Unified Transport Company continued to dominate trade, with shares worth 58,000 dinars changing hands as it rose slightly to 2.15 dinars from 2.14 on Tuesday.

Amad said profit-takers were offloading the share, which rose sharply from around 1.70 dinars last month after Iraq's oil-for-food deal. Transport and industrial companies are expected to do well from increased Iraqi imports.
"It's expected to give an 11 percent dividend so the share could go higher ultimately," Amad said.
Arab Pharmaceuticals, which has good ties with Iraq and is expected to take a stake in sales of extra medicine to Iraq under the U.N. deal, rose strongly to 1.45 dinars from 1.38 dinars.
Gaining shares outnumbered losers by 19 to nine. Shares in 11 companies traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.21 percent to 82.20 points.
